- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- Model underreacts to sentiment shifts in early horizon (e.g., 1–7 days ahead); adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change within 2–3 days of shift.
- For 15–30 day forecasts, model shows persistent mean reversion bias — if 3+ consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should be slightly above trendline to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak or trough.
